title: APQO: An Adaptive Framework for Parametric Query Optimization

statements.text: 1 (Query Template/Query Parameter). 𝑄 is a parametric query template with 𝑑 binding variables. A tuple with 𝑑 binding variables is denoted as a query parameter 𝑣 = (𝛼 1, 𝛼 2, . . . , 𝛼𝑑 ). In this work, each parameter value in 𝑣 is mapped by the database to selectivity, which is then fed into various components of APQO for further processing. Specifically, when preparing training data from historical workload traces, APQO computes parameter selectivity based on the query’s physical execution plan. For table or index scans in a physical query plan, it is the number of returned rows divided by the total rows in the table. For filtering operators, it is the ratio of rows after to before filtering. At runtime, APQO derives selectivity similarly using database statistics and catalog [1]. It is based on the common query optimization technique that estimates predicate selectivities (for point queries, range queries, etc.) using statistical information such as the number of distinct values in columns and histograms [29]. Example 1. Consider the SQL query template: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE price > $1 AND status = $1 A query instance (query) binds parameters $1 and $2 with the values 100 and ’shipped’, respectively. For 𝑣 = [100, ’shipped’], the database maps it to selectivity [0.2, 0.5], where 0.2 and 0.5 are the selectivities for 𝑝𝑟𝑖𝑐𝑒 > 100 and 𝑠𝑡𝑎𝑡𝑢𝑠 = ’shipped’, respectively.
